title: Explaining Fourier analysis with a machine (engineerguy)

moments.sentence: In the previous video, I showed how turning the crank on this machine generates 20 different frequencies, also known as harmonics, which are turned into cosines here, multiplied by coefficients.
magnified and the resulting function plotted here on the front.
For example, if I want to plot a particular function here, how do I set the amplitude bars to produce it?
All of the information that function carries is contained in half a period.
We use the values of these points as the inputs for the machine.
To see how we get these coefficients, we'll look at the side of the machine.
The indices on the rocker arms run from high on the left to low on the right.

bible.summary: The lecture demonstrates how Albert Michelson's harmonic analyzer performs Fourier analysis by decomposing a square wave into sinusoidal coefficients using a mechanical computer.

visual_facts.fact: Title card reads 'Albert Michelson's Harmonic Analyzer Analysis video 3 of 4' and 'Bill Hammack University of Illinois'.
Tall green metal frame with vertical rods, pulleys, gears, chains, and a horizontal bar holding a white rectangular plate.
White rectangular plate on machine front displays a faint waveform.
Text box on right shows 'Albert Michelson's Harmonic Analyzer Synthesis video 2 of 4 previous video'.
Presenter gestures upward along the machine frame.
Green square wave oscillates between 0 and 10 on x-axis labeled -2π, -π, 0, π, 2π.
Yellow bracket marks one period of the square wave.
Vertical line at origin with text stating even functions are mirrored about the origin.
Yellow box highlights the left half period of the square wave.
Sampled square wave shows 11 dots at value 10 for bars 0-10 and 10 dots at value 0 for bars 11-20.
Close-up shows vertical rocker bars with connecting rods; a hand adjusts a bar.
Side view shows crank on left, vertical metal bars, and conical gear assembly.
Numbered tabs on rocker arm tips show 20 on left descending to 1 on right.
Flipped view shows numbers 1 to 20 left to right, with 'low' labels on outer edges and 'high' near center.
All rocker arm tips align in a straight horizontal line; text 'crank 0' appears.
